A1.justification: Both supplied PDFs are readable 23-page versions of FSDC-DETR, with matching sections, equations, figures and tables. Neither includes the cited Supplement A-D or embedded supplementary files; the comparison therefore covers the supplied papers, without judgments about those unavailable materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection results on VisDrone-DET2019 and AITODv2 in Table 1, component and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 2-3, and qualitative detection results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and qualitative detection results reported in v1.

M1.justification: The architecture, DBFSAF, SFS-FF and FSD-Down procedures remain unchanged. Swapping the backbone names before Eq. 1 corrects an inconsistency with the already stated low-frequency ViT/high-frequency CNN roles; it does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both supplied papers evaluate the same small-object detection tasks on VisDrone-DET2019 and AITODv2. The corrected VisDrone image total does not establish different dataset coverage or populations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparison methods and model variants. The RT-DETRv4 and DEIMv2 comparators in the qualitative figures are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the reported VisDrone total from 14,018 to 10,209 images. The training, validation and test counts remain 6,471, 548 and 3,190, whose sum matches the correction. Training budgets, preprocessing and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; no actual resampling or rerun is established.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2, partial-ratio sensitivity analysis in Table 3, frequency-response plots and qualitative comparisons are unchanged in the supplied PDFs.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the detection results. The descriptive dataset statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 4.4 corrects the AITODv2 narrative from 31.1 to 32.3 AP, the gain over DEIMv2-L from 6.4 to 6.6, and the gain over RT-DETRv4-L from 4.7 to 5.5. These now match the unchanged Table 1 values of 32.3, 25.7 and 26.8 AP. No table entries or qualitative results change.

T1.justification: Before Eq. 1, the stated sources of F_L^P and F_H^P are corrected from HGNETv2/DINOv3 to DINOv3/HGNETv2, respectively. This locally corrects the feature-variable definitions; Eqs. 1-13 and the mathematical operations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims, including AP gains of 6.4 and 6.6 and small-object AP gains of 6.8 and 6.9 on the two benchmarks.

C2.justification: The explanations of frequency preservation, component complementarity, localization and generalization remain unchanged. The corrected feature-source sentence aligns with the existing mechanism explanation; no new interpretation, applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same software, hardware, optimizer settings, training schedule and augmentations. The code-access statement and URL are unchanged, and no additional reproducibility material is supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and 93-item bibliography are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds an explicit corresponding-author footnote, changes 'Implement Details' to 'Implementation Details', and makes localized factual corrections. The section order and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added corresponding-author footnote produces a small first-page spacing adjustment. Figures 1-7 and Tables 1-3 retain their displays, captions and locations.

improvement.justification: v3 improves internal consistency: the AITODv2 prose now agrees with Table 1, the VisDrone total matches its stated splits, and the feature-source definitions agree with the existing backbone explanation. These corrections improve accuracy and clarity while retaining the scientific method and experimental evidence.
